info.name: MetaShop API
info.description: MetaShop e-commerce API. Send everything through the API Gateway ({{gatewayUrl}}, :8080) — it validates the JWT, propagates X-User-* headers, adds X-Correlation-Id and rate limits the credential endpoints. The per-service folders ({{authUrl}} :8081, {{productUrl}} :8082) are kept for direct debugging and service-to-service calls. Login first, then copy data.accessToken into the accessToken variable.

item.name: Gateway (entry point :8080)
item.description: Everything the Angular app calls goes through the gateway. It validates the JWT, strips any inbound X-User-* headers, adds X-Correlation-Id and rate limits the credential endpoints. Login through the gateway, copy data.accessToken into the accessToken variable, then the JWT-protected requests below work.

item.name: Inventory Service
item.description: Stock source of truth (:8083). Public availability and the ADMIN endpoints are reachable through the gateway; the Internal folder must be called directly on {{inventoryUrl}} with X-Internal-Token, because /api/v1/internal/** is never routed by the gateway.

item.name: Public
item.description: No authentication. availableQuantity is capped so exact stock is not leaked.

item.name: Admin
item.description: ADMIN role required. Every change is written to the stock_movements audit trail.

item.name: Internal
item.description: Service-to-service, called directly on :8083 (never through the gateway). Requires X-Internal-Token. Responses are plain JSON, not the ApiResponse envelope.

item.name: Cart Service
item.description: One cart per user, owned by the JWT subject. Every endpoint returns the whole cart after a change. Live prices come from product-service and stock from inventory-service, so a 503 here means 'try again shortly' rather than showing a stale price.

item.name: Order Service
item.description: Checkout and the order lifecycle (:8085). An order is created from the caller's cart — the only decision is the shipping address. Prices and the address are frozen as snapshots at checkout; stock is reserved through inventory-service (idempotent per orderId). The lifecycle is CREATED → CONFIRMED (payment) → SHIPPED → DELIVERED, with CANCELLED releasing the stock.

request.description: The amount is read from the order (authoritative, never the request). 201 = captured (order CONFIRMED, cart cleared, stock sold); 200 + success=false = declined (order CANCELLED, stock released). Gateway mode is metashop.payment.gateway-mode on :8086 (SUCCESS / FAILURE / RANDOM).
Same 404 for unknown and foreign orders — ids cannot be probed.
Only orders in CREATED can be paid. Re-run after a capture → 422 (already paid / already confirmed).
Fire twice in parallel against a fresh CREATED order: the loser gets 422 'already in progress'.
The authoritative read payment-service takes the amount and the ownership/status checks from (D-076). Plain JSON, no envelope.

item.name: Notification Service
item.description: The event consumer and email sender (spec 13). It is driven entirely by Kafka: an event on user.events / order.events / payment.events / inventory.events is mapped to a Thymeleaf template, rendered, recorded in notifications, and sent through Spring Mail (Mailpit at http://localhost:8025 in dev). Its only HTTP surface is the admin log below. Nothing else in the stack publishes to Kafka yet, so drive the consumer with kafka-console-producer - and remember it sends ONE RECORD PER LINE.

request.description: Every email this service tried to send, newest first. status is PENDING / SENT / FAILED; a FAILED row is the admin's retry queue. The rendered body is omitted from the list on purpose.
Every email this service tried to send, newest first. status is PENDING / SENT / FAILED; a FAILED row is the admin's retry queue. The rendered body is omitted from the list on purpose.
Every email this service tried to send, newest first. status is PENDING / SENT / FAILED; a FAILED row is the admin's retry queue. The rendered body is omitted from the list on purpose.

item.name: One notification, including the rendered email

request.description: Returns the notification plus the full rendered HTML that was (or will be) sent - the answer to what did the customer actually receive?

Replays the stored subject and body through SMTP once. 200 = sent; 422 if the notification is already SENT (that would duplicate the email); 503 if the mail server refuses again, leaving the row FAILED with the new reason.

description: MetaShop e-commerce API. Send everything through the API Gateway ({{gatewayUrl}}, :8080) — it validates the JWT, propagates X-User-* headers, adds X-Correlation-Id and rate limits the credential endpoints. The per-service folders ({{authUrl}} :8081, {{productUrl}} :8082, {{inventoryUrl}} :8083, {{cartUrl}} :8084, {{orderUrl}} :8085) are kept for direct debugging and service-to-service calls. Login first, then copy data.accessToken into the accessToken variable; service-to-service calls need the internalToken variable in X-Internal-Token.
